steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Greek philosophy began with questioning the nature of the universe; early philosophers sought natural rather than divine explanations | Key Fact: The Sophists were professional teachers who travelled offering instruction in rhetoric and persuasion for pay; they claimed to make the weaker argument appear stronger | Key Fact: Socrates (469-399 BC) challenged assumptions through questioning (the Socratic method/dialectic); he sought truth rather than persuasion | Key Fact: Socrates was tried and executed (399 BC) for impiety and corrupting the youth; his trial illustrates the tension between free thought and Athenian democracy

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on key terms from greek philosophy &amp; thought, and one past-paper question.
